items.explanation_consistent: 해설이 정답·오답 판단과 일치하고 글자 참조가 맞으면 true

items.passage:
Rushes that grow by the black water
When will I see you more?
When will the sorrowful heart forget you,
Land of the green, green shore?
When will the field and the small cabin
See us more
In the old country?

What is to me all the gold yonder?
She that bore me is gone.
Knees that dandled and hands that blessed me
Colder than any stone;
Stranger to me than the face of strangers
Are my own
In the old country.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “Colder than any stone” most nearly suggests that the speaker's mother
options: was strict and unkind to her child
lives in a harsh, wintry place
has died and is beyond the speaker's reach
no longer remembers the speaker
items.explanation: 화자는 '나를 낳은 이가 떠났다'고 말한 뒤, 자신을 어르고 축복하던 무릎과 손이 어떤 돌보다 차갑다고 표현한다. 이는 어머니의 죽음을 뜻하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 '축복하던 손'과 맞지 않는다. B는 실제 날씨로 오해했고, D는 기억 상실을 말하는 근거가 없다.

items.passage: The purpose of the ministry filled him with shame and indignation. Confronted abruptly with the course which four months before had seemed to him natural and proper, the shock brought out the fulness of the change through which he had passed meantime. He has no illusions about Corsica. The inhabitants had disappointed all the expectations of the British,--"At a peace I should rejoice at having given up the island." But the days passing over his head had brought wider and maturer views of the general policy of Great Britain, as well as increasing faith in the powers of the fleet, vigorously used in aggressive warfare.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “the days passing over his head” most nearly suggests
options: the gradual passing of time that broadened his understanding
a series of storms that damaged the fleet
the many orders he received from the ministry
the burden of his growing age and illness
items.explanation: 지문은 그가 넉 달 전에는 자연스럽다고 여긴 방침에 이제 수치를 느낄 만큼 변했다고 한다. 이어 '머리 위로 지나간 날들'이 더 넓고 성숙한 견해와 함대에 대한 믿음을 가져왔다고 하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 폭풍으로 잘못 읽었다. C의 명령과 D의 노화·질병은 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
The heartfelt emotion which thrilled in these words would have softened a woman less self-willed, less hardened in her own caprices than Lady Sarah. As it was, she was only frightened, not touched to tenderness. It was he who was ashamed of the feelings which threatened to overpower him.

Ashamed of his own weakness, and fearing that he was only irritating instead of softening her, he suddenly let her go, and raising her hand to his lips, pressed one tender kiss upon it and then, turning sharply away, felt in his pocket for the keys of his gallery and went out of the study.

Lady Sarah listened a few moments, until she heard the key turn in the gallery door, and knew that her husband had shut himself in with his treasures for the evening.
items.question: Which choice best describes how the tone changes over the course of the text?
options: It moves from playful teasing to joyful reconciliation.
It moves from intense emotion to a quiet, lonely withdrawal.
It moves from cold anger to open celebration.
It moves from calm description to a violent quarrel.
items.explanation: 처음에는 남편의 말에 담긴 진심 어린 감정과 그를 압도하려는 감정이 강하게 드러난다. 그러나 그는 갑자기 그녀를 놓고 서재를 나가 화랑에 혼자 틀어박히며, 사라는 열쇠 소리만 듣는다. 따라서 B가 어조 변화에 맞다. A와 C는 화해·축하가 없으므로 틀렸고, D의 격렬한 다툼도 없다.

items.passage: What great race has ever been won by any man, or by any nation, without some such fall during its course? Have we not all declared that some check to that career was necessary? Men in their pursuit of intelligence had forgotten to be honest; in struggling for greatness they had discarded purity. The nation has been great, but the statesmen of the nation have been little. Men have hardly been ambitious to govern, but they have coveted the wages of governors. Corruption has crept into high places,--into places that should have been high,--till of all holes and corners in the land they have become the lowest. No public man has been trusted for ordinary honesty.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From bitter resentment of a rival nation to cautious praise of its leaders
From playful mockery of statesmen to sincere sympathy for their burdens
From hopeful anticipation of reform to quiet resignation about failure
From reflective acceptance of a setback to blunt condemnation of corruption
items.explanation: 지문 앞부분은 수사 의문문으로 어떤 경주에도 넘어짐은 있으며 그 제동이 필요했다고 차분히 받아들인다. 이후 정치가들이 작았고 부패가 높은 자리에 스며들었다는 문장에서 어조가 날카로운 비판으로 바뀐다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A의 경쟁 국가, B의 조롱과 동정, C의 개혁에 대한 기대는 지문에 나타나지 않는다.

items.passage:
Upon mentioning this I found that it had been noticed in elm avenues and groups a hundred miles distant, so that it is not a local circumstance.

As far as yet appears, the elms do not seem materially injured, the damage being outwardly confined to the bough attacked. These brown spots looked very remarkable just after the trees had become green. They were quite distinct from the damage caused by the snow of October 1880. The boughs broken by the snow had leaves upon them which at once turned brown, and in the case of the oak were visible, the following spring, as brown spots among the green.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It notes that a tree condition is widespread, assesses its effects, and separates it from earlier damage.
It explains the cause of a tree disease, then proposes a method for preventing its spread.
It recalls a snowstorm in detail, then argues that the storm permanently weakened the elms.
It compares elms and oaks in general, then concludes that oaks are the hardier trees.
items.explanation: 화자는 먼저 갈색 반점이 백 마일 떨어진 곳에서도 관찰되어 지역적 현상이 아니라고 밝힌다. 이어 느릅나무가 크게 손상되지 않았다고 평가하고, 1880년 10월 눈 피해와는 뚜렷이 다르다고 구분한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 원인·예방책, C의 영구적 약화 주장, D의 수종 비교는 지문에 없다.

items.passage: Really, Sir Hugo was worthy of it on his own individual merits. He was a fine young fellow. The foundation of his principles had been laid by a good mother--a widow who had never ceased to mourn for the husband of her youth, whose son, her only child, was the apple of her eye. From her he had derived a remarkable amount of ingenuousness and a dash of enthusiasm, which such intercourse with the world as he had commanded had failed to extinguish. He was regarded as something of a young Quixote at his University, which had been his world for the most part, but he had possessed wit to defend his views. He was manly, rather rash, and a little thoughtless; but in his very thoughtlessness he was generous and honest--a lad to be liked first and trusted afterwards.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes a mother's grief, then shows how her sorrow eventually ruined her son.
It asserts a young man's merit, traces the source of his principles, and summarizes his traits.
It recounts a university quarrel, then explains how a young man was punished for it.
It lists a young man's faults, then reveals that others refused to trust him.
items.explanation: 지문은 먼저 휴고 경이 자신의 장점만으로도 그럴 자격이 있다고 단언한다. 이어 그의 원칙의 토대가 어머니에게서 왔다고 설명하고, 마지막에 성급함과 관대함 같은 성격을 요약한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 몰락, C의 처벌, D의 불신은 지문 내용과 어긋난다.

items.passage:
We cannot suppose that life would develop in any important degree in a region of perpetual frost, such as the polar regions of our globe. But we do not find any end to it as the climate becomes warmer. On the contrary, every one knows that the tropics are the most fertile regions of the globe in its production. The luxuriance of the vegetation and the number of the animals continually increase the more tropical the climate becomes. Where the limit may be set no one can say. But it would doubtless be far above the present temperature of the equatorial regions.

It has often been said that this does not apply to the human race, that men lack vigor in the tropics.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes polar wildlife, then argues that cold regions support the most life.
It questions whether tropical regions exist, then defends that claim with examples.
It presents a claim linking warmth to abundant life, then introduces an objection about humans.
It praises human vigor in the tropics, then explains why vegetation is scarce there.
items.explanation: 글쓴이는 영구 동토에서는 생명이 발달하기 어렵지만 기후가 따뜻할수록 동식물이 늘어난다고 주장한다. 그 뒤 새 문단에서 이 원리가 인류에는 적용되지 않는다는, 열대에서 사람이 활력을 잃는다는 반론을 소개한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A, B, D는 지문의 주장과 반대이거나 근거가 없다.

items.passage: When I arrived at home I of course went to see Lottie before talking with any one else. I found my darling all that heart could wish. She was more beautiful, more charming in my eyes than ever. The large, dreamy blue eyes were swimming in tears of joy as I held her to my glad heart, and I saw a look of love that satisfied me that I was the possessor of a treasure of great value. I lingered by my darling’s side until late at night. Every little trifling incident was described--the days of old were alluded to and discussed, while the present and future came in for a full share.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Lottie?
options: Deep affection and delight in her company
Polite respect mixed with quiet doubt
Mild irritation at her emotional display
Guilty unease about his long absence
items.explanation: 화자는 집에 오자마자 다른 누구보다 먼저 로티를 찾아가 그녀가 마음에 바라던 모든 것이라고 말한다. 또 밤늦게까지 그녀 곁에 머물며 지난날과 미래를 이야기했다고 서술한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. 의심, 짜증, 죄책감을 보여 주는 표현은 지문에 없으므로 B, C, D는 틀리다.

items.passage: We had sunk together into the slough of despond, and she contrived to scramble out of it and leave me in the mire. She was clever enough to make use of me to accomplish her escape, sent me out among hard-hearted humanity to borrow, beg, or steal the means by which she meant to separate herself from my fallen fortunes. Do you think I came across the world to seek for her? No, Dick, I am not such a fool. I have been cheated once. I shall never be her dupe again. Do you think I could ever trust her any more?--that if fortune smiled upon us, and she pretended to love me, I could feel any confidence in her truth, any security in her affection?
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The speaker hopes to find the woman and win back her love.
The speaker blames himself alone for their shared misfortune.
The speaker insists he will never again trust a woman who deceived him.
The speaker asks Dick to help him borrow money for a journey.
items.explanation: 화자는 그녀가 자신을 이용해 빠져나갔고 자신은 진창에 남겨졌다고 말한다. 이어 그녀를 찾으러 온 것이 아니며 다시는 속지 않겠다고 하고, 앞으로 그녀의 진심을 믿을 수 없다고 묻는다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 반대이고, B는 그녀를 탓하는 태도와 어긋나며, D는 과거 사건을 잘못 쓴 것이다.

items.passage: Eight miles meant nearly three hours’ steaming for us, and I could also see suspicious ripples at the upper end of the reach. Nevertheless, I was annoyed beyond expression at the delay, and most unreasonably, too, since one night more could not matter much after so many months. As we had plenty of wood, and caution was the word, I brought up in the middle of the stream. The reach was narrow, straight, with high sides like a railway cutting. The dusk came gliding into it long before the sun had set. The current ran smooth and swift, but a dumb immobility sat on the banks.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a dumb immobility sat on the banks” most nearly suggests that the riverbanks
options: were crowded with people waiting silently
were too steep for the boat to approach
were slowly being worn away by the current
were eerily silent and still
items.explanation: 화자는 해가 지기 전부터 어둠이 좁은 수로에 스며들었다고 묘사한다. 물살은 빠르게 흘렀지만 강둑에는 말없는 정적이 앉아 있었다는 대비로 섬뜩한 고요함을 드러낸다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A의 사람들, B의 경사, C의 침식은 구절의 의미가 아니다.

items.passage:
"I had grottos, and fountains, and orange-tree groves,
I had all that enchantment has told;
I had sweet shady walks for the gods and their loves,
I had mountains of coral and gold.

"But a storm that I felt not had risen and rolled,
While wrapped in a slumber I lay;
And when I looked out in the morning, behold,
My Castle was carried away.

"It passed over rivers and valleys and groves,
The world it was all in my view;
I thought of my friends, of their fates, of their loves,
And often, full often, of you.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “My Castle was carried away” most nearly suggests that the speaker
options: lost the splendid world of the imagination
fled from a real fortress during a storm
gave away riches to friends
moved to a new home in the mountains
items.explanation: 화자는 동굴, 분수, 산호와 황금의 산 등 마법 같은 것들을 가졌다고 나열한다. 그러나 잠든 사이 일어난 폭풍에 성이 날아갔다고 하며, 그 성은 상상 속 화려한 꿈을 가리킨다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B, C, D는 비유를 문자 그대로 읽거나 근거 없는 해석이다.

items.passage: Conrad Dasipodius was a man for whom the simplest objects of daily life had borne a significance. It had been his nature to see “sermons in stones, and good in everything”; and could he have looked on this scene before him, with all its wedded glory of nature and of art, he must have found in it some anodyne for the gnawing pain of hope disappointed. But he could have no part now in such joys, and to him the world was a dull leaden-hued wilderness. Winter and summer, day and night, in all the years to come, the same. A dismal chaos, a dark and thorny way indeed, where love and friendship had left him in his utmost need, to blunder on alone.
items.question: Which choice best describes how the tone of the text shifts?
options: From mild amusement to quiet pride in Conrad's achievements
From harsh criticism to gentle forgiveness of Conrad's faults
From restless anticipation to calm contentment with the scene
From appreciation of Conrad's outlook to bleak desolation
items.explanation: 처음에는 일상의 사물에서도 의미를 찾던 Conrad의 기질을 긍정적으로 묘사한다. 그러나 'But he could have no part now in such joys' 이후 세상이 '납빛 황무지'가 되었다는 절망적 어조로 바뀌므로 D가 정답이다. A와 C는 후반의 어두운 분위기와 맞지 않는다. B는 Conrad를 비판하는 부분이 없어 틀리다.

items.passage:
The girl, tall and strong, walking with the ease that comes from health and a steadfast mind; the eager, restless boy running and jumping by her side. Barebone must have seen them as soon as they saw him. They were part of Farlingford, these two. He had a sudden feeling of having been away for years, with this difference--that he came back and found nothing changed. Whereas, in reality, he who returns after a long absence usually finds no one awaiting him.

He did as Sep had foretold--crossing to the far side of the river, and then gaining the mouth of the creek in one tack.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes two figures, gives Barebone's reflection on returning, then shows him sailing.
It recounts a quarrel between two figures, then explains why Barebone left the town.
It praises Farlingford's landscape, then lists the changes Barebone finds on his return.
It presents Sep's warning about the river, then describes the girl's response to it.
items.explanation: 지문은 먼저 소녀와 소년의 모습을 묘사하고, 이어 Barebone이 오랜 부재 후 아무것도 변하지 않았다고 느끼는 생각을 제시한 뒤, 마지막에 그가 강을 건너 배를 모는 행동으로 넘어간다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 다툼, C의 변화 목록은 지문에 없다. D는 Sep의 예언이 마지막에 짧게 언급될 뿐 글의 출발점이 아니므로 틀리다.

items.passage: The dawn was breaking, and at its first sign the escort of Saladin’s soldiers had turned and left them, saying that now they were safe in their own country. All night they had ridden fast and far. The plain was behind them, and their road ran among hills. Suddenly it turned, and in the flaming lights of the new-born day showed them a sight so beautiful that for a moment all that little company drew rein to gaze. For yonder before them, though far away as yet, throned upon her hills, stood the holy city of Jerusalem.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It explains why the escort left, then describes a battle with Saladin's soldiers.
It recounts a night's journey into the hills, then reveals a striking view of Jerusalem.
It describes Jerusalem in detail, then recalls the hardships of reaching the city.
It contrasts the plain with the hills, then explains why the company turned back.
items.explanation: 지문은 호위대가 떠나고 밤새 달려 언덕길에 들어선 여정을 먼저 서술한다. 이어 길이 꺾이며 새벽빛 속에 예루살렘이 나타나는 장면으로 마무리되므로 B가 정답이다. A의 전투, D의 회군은 지문에 없다. C는 순서가 반대이며 도시를 자세히 묘사하지도 않는다.

items.passage: At the supper-table he talked much and well, exceedingly well, I thought, except when he touched on the war, which he was continually doing, and then I was on tenter-hooks. His point of view was so opposed to ours as to threaten in several instances to bring on an engagement all along the line. This calamity was averted by my passing something to him at the critical moment. Now I checked his advance by a slice of cold tongue, and now I turned his flank with another cup of tea; but I questioned my ability to preserve peace throughout the evening. Before the meal was at an end there had crept into Clara's manner a polite calmness which I never liked to see.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward the supper conversation?
options: Bored indifference to the guest's lengthy remarks about the war
Open hostility toward the guest's opinions about the war
Delighted admiration for Clara's skill in calming the guest
Anxious but wry watchfulness over a dispute about to erupt
items.explanation: 화자는 손님이 전쟁 이야기를 할 때마다 '바늘방석'에 앉은 듯했다고 말한다. 또 혀 요리와 차 한 잔으로 그의 '진격을 막고 측면을 돌렸다'고 전쟁 비유를 써 자신의 노력을 익살스럽게 묘사하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 화자가 대화를 잘 들었다고 칭찬해 틀리다. B는 화자가 오히려 평화를 지키려 하고, C는 Clara가 차갑게 변한 것을 싫어하므로 틀리다.

items.passage:
There was no time to protest or to ask questions. And Juliette felt herself passed on from one pair of strong arms to another, until she was standing on the deck under the humming rigging, surrounded by men who seemed huge in their gleaming oil-skins.

"This way, mademoiselle," said one, who was even larger than the others, in English, of which she understood enough to catch his meaning. "I will take you to your father. Show a light this way, one of you."

His fingers closed round her arm, and he led her, unconscious of a strength that almost lifted her from her feet, toward an open door, where a lamp burnt dimly within.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Juliette argues with the sailors before agreeing to board.
Juliette struggles to understand the sailors' foreign speech.
Juliette is brought aboard and led toward her father.
Juliette searches the deck alone for a lamp and a door.
items.explanation: Juliette는 질문할 틈도 없이 여러 팔에 넘겨져 갑판에 서게 되고, 가장 큰 선원이 아버지에게 데려가겠다며 그녀를 문 쪽으로 이끈다. 이 두 장면을 합치면 C가 요지이다. A는 '항의할 시간이 없었다'는 서술과 어긋난다. B는 그녀가 뜻을 이해했다고 하므로 틀리고, D는 그녀가 혼자가 아니라 이끌려 간다.

items.passage: I bent my head, and seemed to receive the Atlantic on my back. The world seemed going to destruction. I could not see anything, the flood poured down savagely. I raised my head, with open mouth, and the most of the American cataract went down my throat. If I had sprung a leak now I had been lost. And at this moment I discovered that the bridge had ceased, and we must trust for a foothold to the slippery and precipitous rocks. I never was so scared before and survived it. But we got through at last, and emerged into the open day, where we could stand in front of the laced and frothy and seething world of descending water, and look at it.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “receive the Atlantic on my back” most nearly suggests
options: the overwhelming weight of the falling water
the narrator's wish to swim across the ocean
the chill of a sea breeze along the bridge
the narrator's pride in carrying heavy loads
items.explanation: 화자는 고개를 숙이자 대서양을 등에 받는 것 같았고 세상이 무너지는 듯하며 물이 '사납게' 쏟아졌다고 말한다. 따라서 이 구절은 쏟아지는 물의 압도적인 양과 무게를 과장해 표현한 것이므로 A가 정답이다. B의 수영, C의 바닷바람은 실제 대서양으로 오해한 것이다. D는 무거운 것을 나르는 자부심과 무관하며 화자는 오히려 겁에 질려 있다.

items.passage: I slipped through one of these cracks, went up a swept and ungarnished staircase, as arid as a desert, and opened the first door I came to. Two women, one fat and the other slim, sat on straw-bottomed chairs, knitting black wool. The slim one got up and walked straight at me—still knitting with downcast eyes—and only just as I began to think of getting out of her way, as you would for a somnambulist, stood still, and looked up. Her dress was as plain as an umbrella-cover, and she turned round without a word and preceded me into a waiting-room. I gave my name, and looked about. Deal table in the middle, plain chairs all round the walls, on one end a large shining map, marked with all the colours of a rainbow.

### lit40-easy-04-019 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift

[지문]

Men have hardly been ambitious to govern, but they have coveted the wages of governors. ### lit40-easy-04-044 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 text_structure
[지문]
The girl, tall and strong, walking with the ease that comes from health and a steadfast mind; the eager, restless boy running and jumping by her side. Barebone must have seen them as soon as they saw him. They were part of Farlingford, these two. He had a sudden feeling of having been away for years, with this difference--that he came back and found nothing changed. Whereas, in reality, he who returns after a long absence usually finds no one awaiting him.

He did as Sep had foretold--crossing to the far side of the river, and then gaining the mouth of the creek in one tack.

[질문] Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
A) It describes two figures, gives Barebone's reflection on returning, then shows him sailing.
B) It recounts a quarrel between two figures, then explains why Barebone left the town.
C) It praises Farlingford's landscape, then lists the changes Barebone finds on his return.
D) It presents Sep's warning about the river, then describes the girl's response to it.

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
지문은 먼저 소녀와 소년의 모습을 묘사하고, 이어 Barebone이 오랜 부재 후 아무것도 변하지 않았다고 느끼는 생각을 제시한 뒤, 마지막에 그가 강을 건너 배를 모는 행동으로 넘어간다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 다툼, C의 변화 목록은 지문에 없다. D는 Sep의 예언이 마지막에 짧게 언급될 뿐 글의 출발점이 아니므로 틀리다.
### lit40-easy-04-045 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 text_structure
[지문]
The dawn was breaking, and at its first sign the escort of Saladin’s soldiers had turned and left them, saying that now they were safe in their own country. All night they had ridden fast and far. The plain was behind them, and their road ran among hills. Suddenly it turned, and in the flaming lights of the new-born day showed them a sight so beautiful that for a moment all that little company drew rein to gaze. For yonder before them, though far away as yet, throned upon her hills, stood the holy city of Jerusalem.

[질문] Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
A) It explains why the escort left, then describes a battle with Saladin's soldiers.
B) It recounts a night's journey into the hills, then reveals a striking view of Jerusalem.
C) It describes Jerusalem in detail, then recalls the hardships of reaching the city.
D) It contrasts the plain with the hills, then explains why the company turned back.

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
지문은 호위대가 떠나고 밤새 달려 언덕길에 들어선 여정을 먼저 서술한다. 이어 길이 꺾이며 새벽빛 속에 예루살렘이 나타나는 장면으로 마무리되므로 B가 정답이다. A의 전투, D의 회군은 지문에 없다. C는 순서가 반대이며 도시를 자세히 묘사하지도 않는다.
### lit40-easy-04-048 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]
At the supper-table he talked much and well, exceedingly well, I thought, except when he touched on the war, which he was continually doing, and then I was on tenter-hooks. His point of view was so opposed to ours as to threaten in several instances to bring on an engagement all along the line. This calamity was averted by my passing something to him at the critical moment. Now I checked his advance by a slice of cold tongue, and now I turned his flank with another cup of tea; but I questioned my ability to preserve peace throughout the evening. Before the meal was at an end there had crept into Clara's manner a polite calmness which I never liked to see.

[질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward the supper conversation?
A) Bored indifference to the guest's lengthy remarks about the war
B) Open hostility toward the guest's opinions about the war
C) Delighted admiration for Clara's skill in calming the guest
D) Anxious but wry watchfulness over a dispute about to erupt

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
화자는 손님이 전쟁 이야기를 할 때마다 '바늘방석'에 앉은 듯했다고 말한다. 또 혀 요리와 차 한 잔으로 그의 '진격을 막고 측면을 돌렸다'고 전쟁 비유를 써 자신의 노력을 익살스럽게 묘사하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 화자가 대화를 잘 들었다고 칭찬해 틀리다. B는 화자가 오히려 평화를 지키려 하고, C는 Clara가 차갑게 변한 것을 싫어하므로 틀리다.
### lit40-easy-04-051 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose
[지문]
There was no time to protest or to ask questions. And Juliette felt herself passed on from one pair of strong arms to another, until she was standing on the deck under the humming rigging, surrounded by men who seemed huge in their gleaming oil-skins.

"This way, mademoiselle," said one, who was even larger than the others, in English, of which she understood enough to catch his meaning. "I will take you to your father. Show a light this way, one of you."

His fingers closed round her arm, and he led her, unconscious of a strength that almost lifted her from her feet, toward an open door, where a lamp burnt dimly within.

[질문] Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
A) Juliette argues with the sailors before agreeing to board.
B) Juliette struggles to understand the sailors' foreign speech.
C) Juliette is brought aboard and led toward her father.
D) Juliette searches the deck alone for a lamp and a door.

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
Juliette는 질문할 틈도 없이 여러 팔에 넘겨져 갑판에 서게 되고, 가장 큰 선원이 아버지에게 데려가겠다며 그녀를 문 쪽으로 이끈다. 이 두 장면을 합치면 C가 요지이다. A는 '항의할 시간이 없었다'는 서술과 어긋난다. B는 그녀가 뜻을 이해했다고 하므로 틀리고, D는 그녀가 혼자가 아니라 이끌려 간다.
### lit40-easy-04-052 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
I bent my head, and seemed to receive the Atlantic on my back. The world seemed going to destruction. I could not see anything, the flood poured down savagely. I raised my head, with open mouth, and the most of the American cataract went down my throat. If I had sprung a leak now I had been lost. And at this moment I discovered that the bridge had ceased, and we must trust for a foothold to the slippery and precipitous rocks. I never was so scared before and survived it. But we got through at last, and emerged into the open day, where we could stand in front of the laced and frothy and seething world of descending water, and look at it.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “receive the Atlantic on my back” most nearly suggests
A) the overwhelming weight of the falling water
B) the narrator's wish to swim across the ocean
C) the chill of a sea breeze along the bridge
D) the narrator's pride in carrying heavy loads

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
화자는 고개를 숙이자 대서양을 등에 받는 것 같았고 세상이 무너지는 듯하며 물이 '사납게' 쏟아졌다고 말한다. 따라서 이 구절은 쏟아지는 물의 압도적인 양과 무게를 과장해 표현한 것이므로 A가 정답이다. B의 수영, C의 바닷바람은 실제 대서양으로 오해한 것이다. D는 무거운 것을 나르는 자부심과 무관하며 화자는 오히려 겁에 질려 있다.
### lit40-easy-04-053 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
I slipped through one of these cracks, went up a swept and ungarnished staircase, as arid as a desert, and opened the first door I came to. Two women, one fat and the other slim, sat on straw-bottomed chairs, knitting black wool. The slim one got up and walked straight at me—still knitting with downcast eyes—and only just as I began to think of getting out of her way, as you would for a somnambulist, stood still, and looked up. Her dress was as plain as an umbrella-cover, and she turned round without a word and preceded me into a waiting-room. I gave my name, and looked about. Deal table in the middle, plain chairs all round the walls, on one end a large shining map, marked with all the colours of a rainbow.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “as arid as a desert” most nearly suggests
A) a place made dangerous by heat and dust
B) a space that is bare and without warmth
C) a building located in a remote dry region
D) a stairway too steep and long to climb

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
구절 바로 앞의 'swept and ungarnished'는 계단이 깨끗이 쓸렸지만 아무 장식도 없음을 보여 준다. 이어지는 평범한 의자, 우산 덮개 같은 옷차림 묘사도 삭막한 분위기를 이어 가므로 B가 정답이다. A와 C는 사막을 문자 그대로 받아들인 해석이다. D는 계단의 경사나 길이에 대한 언급이 없어 틀리다.
### lit40-easy-04-055 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
One last word about our amiable author. His great book remains eminently alive, and wields after two centuries and a half a permanent influence. When you refer to it, you must not expect a logical development of philosophical theory. We do not look to find a system in a book of maxims and portraits. La Bruyere was a moralist, pure and simple; he awakened sensibility, he encouraged refinement, and he exposed the vicious difference which existed around him--and which no one else had seemed to notice--that the possession of more or fewer pieces of money made between human beings otherwise equal.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “eminently alive” most nearly suggests that the book
A) is filled with vivid scenes of physical action
B) describes its author's long and healthy life
C) was recently rediscovered after being lost
D) continues to be widely read and influential

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
구절 바로 뒤에 이 책이 두 세기 반이 지난 뒤에도 '영구적인 영향력'을 행사한다는 설명이 이어진다. 따라서 '살아 있다'는 말은 책이 여전히 읽히고 영향력을 가진다는 뜻이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 이 책이 격언과 인물 묘사로 이루어졌다는 설명과 맞지 않는다. B는 '살아 있음'을 작가의 생애로 오해했고, C의 재발견은 언급되지 않는다.
### lit40-easy-04-056 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
I took off its hat and cloak to see if there were any strings cutting its neck or choking it. Then I glanced at the feet, and lo! there was the trouble. The boots were at least one size too small. I took them off, and the stockings, too, and found the feet as cold as ice and the prints of the stockings clearly traced on the tender flesh. We all know the agony of tight boots. I rubbed the feet and held them in my hands until they were warm, when the poor little thing fell asleep.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “as cold as ice” most nearly suggests that the child's feet were
A) painfully chilled from poor circulation
B) unusually hard and stiff from walking
C) frozen solid after a winter accident
D) pale because the stockings were white

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
화자는 신발이 한 치수 이상 작았고 발에 스타킹 자국이 깊게 남아 있었다고 말한다. 화자가 발을 문지르고 손으로 감싸 따뜻해지자 아이가 잠들었으므로, 이 구절은 꽉 끼는 신발 때문에 발이 몹시 차가워졌음을 나타낸다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B와 D는 얼음의 단단함이나 색으로 잘못 해석한 것이다. C의 사고는 지문에 없다.
